note: Rewritten from the diagnostic comparative account of this species in Emerson 1960 (American Museum Novitates No. 1988, 'New Termitinae from the Ethiopian Region'); the original is in English. That paper is a genus-level revision and does not give a formal species-level description of this species within the source pack (Williams 1954 originally recorded it as Procubitermes planifacies), so only the sentences that directly describe the morphology of this species are taken, not the purely intergeneric inferential ones. The source pack continues from line 194 with Nitiditermes berghei, new species, which is not this species and was not used.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: the upper and lower surfaces of the mandibles from the marginal teeth to the apex are finely granulated, and in suitable light fine striae are visible near the apex and near the marginal teeth, in accordance with the characters of the genus Lepidotermes. The tooth-like process on the molar plate of the left mandible projects less far forwards than in L. goliathi but farther than in Nitiditermes berghei. The median concavity of the labrum is less deep than in N. berghei and its lateral points less sharp. The postmentum of the soldier is irregular in lateral view and the frons steeper in lateral view. Alate—worker: the distance from the apex of the left mandible to the first marginal tooth is about equal to the distance from the tip of the first marginal tooth to the tip of the third marginal tooth; on this basis the author considered that the species may belong to a new genus close to Fastigitermes.
